title: EFC Background No-Go Theorem: Why Background-Level Modification Cannot Suppress Structure Growth
abstract: Consolidation package establishing the background sector no-go theorem for Energy-Flow Cosmology. Three independent lines of evidence — an analytical sign lemma (ΔE² ≤ 0 for all z > 0), numerical CLASS v3.3.4 verification, and observational CMB+BAO joint constraints (α → 0) — demonstrate that the EFC background coupling channel cannot suppress σ₈ and is observationally empty. This structural boundary redirects all late-time EFC effects to the perturbation sector (μ, Σ, η), producing sharper and independently testable predictions.

efc_context.regime_relevance: L0–L2 background sector; establishes that background gate is structurally excluded for growth suppression, redirecting EFC to perturbation sector
efc_context.epistemic_layer: Layer B (analytical theorem + numerical verification + observational confirmation)

key_results: Sign lemma: ΔE²(z) = A·[g(z) − g(0)] ≤ 0 for all z > 0 under closure normalisation E(0) = 1
Corollary: H_EFC(z) ≤ H_ΛCDM(z) → background modification enhances growth, cannot suppress σ₈
CLASS v3.3.4 verification: ΔH/H = −0.3% to −1.1%, negative everywhere
Growth enhancement: fσ₈ increased by +0.50% to +0.76% (opposite direction from S₈ tension)
Observational: α collapses to ≈ 0 under all Planck+BAO combinations (|Δχ²| < 2σ)
α–H₀ degeneracy correlation = 0.975; CMB is blind to α, BAO breaks the degeneracy
Background sector is structurally excluded and observationally empty
All EFC effects must enter through perturbation sector: μ ≈ 0.94, Σ ≈ 1.05, η ≈ 1.10
